headline.label: of organizations use AI regularly in at least one business function
headline.detail: Global survey of executives, up from 78% a year earlier.

headline.label: higher advertised pay in job postings that ask for AI skills
headline.detail: About $18,000 a year more, from an analysis of 1.3 billion postings; 43% higher with two or more AI skills.

headline.label: of postings that ask for AI skills are outside IT and computer science
headline.detail: Postings mentioning generative AI skills in non-tech roles grew about 800% from 2022 to 2024.

headline.label: of leaders say they would not hire someone without AI skills
headline.detail: 71% would rather hire a less experienced candidate who has AI skills than a more experienced one who does not. Survey of 31,000 people in 31 countries.

growth.title: Projected U.S. employment growth, 2025 to 2035
growth.subtitle: Percent change in employment for occupations that use the skills this program teaches, against all occupations. Median annual wage, May 2025, where published.
growth.note: BLS expects AI to add demand for building models, analyzing data and integrating applications into business practice, and to reduce demand in some arts and design, sales and administrative roles. Computer and mathematical occupations are projected to grow 10.1% over 2024–34, more than three times the all-occupation rate.

countries.title: Share of job postings that mention AI skills, 2025
countries.subtitle: Percent of all postings in each labor market. The United States is highlighted.

regional.label: AI job postings in California in 2025, about 17% of the U.S. total
regional.detail: The most of any state; Texas (80,547) and New York (66,029) follow.

regional.label: largest AI-specialist workforce in North America: Los Angeles and Orange County
regional.detail: 13,605 AI specialists, behind only San Francisco, Seattle and New York.

regional.label: mean hourly wage for computer and mathematical occupations in Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim
regional.detail: Against $37.15 for all occupations in the metro area and $33.54 nationwide, May 2025.

regional.label: job openings projected in Los Angeles County over 2022–2032
regional.detail: 608,800 from growth and 1,032,000 from replacement needs; professional and business services adds 81,200 jobs.

regionalNote: Orange County's 2026 Labor Market Overview projects healthcare, the county's largest growth sector, to add 49,771 jobs by 2035, with aerospace and defense, the clean economy, life sciences and high tech adding about 8,000 more. The Los Angeles and Orange County Centers of Excellence publish the regional labor-market research California's community colleges use for program planning.

global.label: net new jobs worldwide by 2030: 170 million created, 92 million displaced
global.detail: Employers expect 39% of workers' skills to change by 2030, and 63% name skills gaps as their main barrier. AI and big data is the fastest-growing skill.

global.label: jobs worldwide has some exposure to generative AI
global.detail: 34% in high-income countries. Clerical work is the most exposed; the likely effect is transformation of jobs, not replacement.

global.label: average wage premium for AI skills, across a billion job ads on six continents
global.detail: Up from 57% the year before. Jobs that require AI skills grew 69% against 9% for all jobs.

global.label: of employers in manufacturing and finance name a lack of skills as the main barrier to adopting AI
global.detail: Over half report a growing need for highly skilled workers; over half of small and mid-sized firms do not yet use generative AI.

latest.label: Latest U.S. jobs report, August 2026
latest.text: Payrolls rose by 162,000 and unemployment held at 4.1%. The information industry lost jobs. A monthly reading, revised twice; it is context, not a trend.
